newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end down one percent.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end down one percent.

text.p: Swiss shares fell sharply on Friday, hit by declines in U.S. markets following release of stronger than expected economic data.
Shares ended down one roughly percent, and near the day's lows. Several shares with a heavy weighting in the blue-chip SMI index were under pressure.
Few investors were willing to take positions ahead of the Labor Day weekend in the U.S. Volumes were generally modest.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended down 36.3 points, or 0.99 percent, at 3,646.3.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) fell 18.04 points, or 0.76 percent, to 2,342.99.

CS Holding, which led the actives list, fell 3.75 francs to 124.50, a slump of nearly three percent. Speculative selling by investors who had hoped for a faster pace of restructuring may have been a factor in CS Holding's declines, traders said.
UBS bearer shares and SBC lost 1.27 percent each to 1,165 francs and 233.75 francs, respectively.
Swiss Re consolidated after recent strong gains, falling 10 francs to 1,297. Winterthur gave up more than two percent to 735 francs. Zurich shares were also markedly lower.
Pharmaceuticals Roche, Ciba and Sandoz also lost ground.
Swissair was up seven francs, closing at 1,097, after it reported a narrower half-year loss earlier in the day.
Swissair's chief financial officer Georges Schorderet said the airline's expectations for full-year results will be revised downward slightly due to lower-than-expected traffic figures.
